Per the registered H3 analysis plan (osf/preregistration.md:519-521: 'Compare single-pass mean F1 vs voted F1 at each (N, threshold) combination' + 'Generate threshold sweep curves' + 'Identify optimal (N, threshold)'), the headline is each configuration's BEST (N, threshold) operating point against the known test-tile ground truth -- the study's purpose is to characterise how well VLM symbol extraction localises mounds, so best-achievable performance is the deliverable, not a confound. Method: round-robin tile-swap permutation (10k perms, seed 42, two-sided; BH-FDR q=0.05) + greedy-clique tiering over a 22-cell board (4 consensus champions + 18 single-pass cells); 197/231 pairs significant -> 7 tiers. (1) DIVERSITY DIVIDEND (post-hoc; unregistered thinking factor) -- HIGH-thinking consensus significantly exceeds minimal-thinking consensus at matched modality: text +0.153 F1 (BH-p<0.001; MCC +0.239) and image +0.070 F1 (BH-p<0.001; MCC +0.272). The HIGH-thinking pools take the larger consensus gain -- more varied proposals let a high vote threshold prune their false positives. (2) CONSENSUS vs SINGLE-PASS -- every consensus champion significantly beats its matched within-pool single-pass baseline (+0.13 to +0.43 F1, all BH-p<0.001), and the lift persists at the production N=5 operating point (text 4-of-5, image 3-of-5; +0.09 to +0.33 F1). Cheap Flash consensus reaches the expensive Pro single-pass tier on localisation F1. OPERATING-POINT SENSITIVITY (characterised, co-headlined): the Tier-1 parity is at the best (N, threshold) point (26-of-30); at the production N=5 carry-forward point (text 4-of-5) the same pool reaches TIER 2 (0.720), tying genuine Pro text at T=0.7 -- a best-minus-N5 delta of ~0.094 F1 (the within-test cousin of the carry-forward-vs-best delta the 55-map generalisation reports). F1-parity is NOT MCC-parity: the Pro text leaders are more tile-precise (MCC 0.790, 11 tile FPs) than the Flash consensus champion (MCC 0.620, 41 tile FPs) -- the metric-dependent-winner pattern of the n1 board persists. Deployment generalisation to unseen maps is the separate question answered by the 55-map runs. Era-2 487-tile test scope, 384px, gemini-3-flash. | tile-size-sweep | sweep | 35 | registered-exploratory | Results | Tile-size characterisation across 256/384/512 px (F1@20m), gemini-3-flash, GS 4-map curator GT. The optimal tile size is ARCHITECTURE-DEPENDENT, consistent with the FP-filtering mechanism (Obs 351, Obs 179, Obs 171). CLEAN ISOLATION (hold architecture x modality x thinking x temperature constant, vary only size): single-pass text climbs monotonically with tile size (256=0.342 < 384=0.520 < 512=0.606) -- with no FP filter, larger tiles give cleaner proposals; single-pass image is flat (384~0.600 ~ 512~0.586). Text MINIMAL consensus still prefers 512 (+0.02..+0.05 over 384 across T0.3/0.7/1.0) -- a weak filter. Text HIGH consensus FLIPS to 384 (T0.7 0.814 > 512 0.773; T0.3 0.789 > 0.774; T1.0 ~tie) -- the strong diversity+vote filter realises 384's higher recall. CONSENSUS+VERIFIER head-to-head (View 3; Stage-D carry-forward adversarial verifier, gemini-3-flash minimal T=0.0 n=1; 14-buf+MCC; best prob_t per cell): 384=0.890 > 256=0.856 > 512=0.793 -- best=384px (delta +0.034 over 256). Two findings: (1) 384 STILL leads at consensus+PV, as it does at consensus-only, confirming the Obs 179 prior (NOT a surprise); (2) the verifier RESCUES 256 (Obs 352): 256 consensus jumps from 0.460 consensus-only (WORST) to 0.856 consensus+PV (+0.396), LEAPFROGGING 512 to take second -- so the per-architecture order is single-pass 512>384>256, consensus-only 384>512>256, consensus+PV 384>256>512. Obs 351's open question -- does 256 overwhelm even the verifier? -- is now answered: NO, the verifier rescues 256, but 384 retains the lead. CAVEAT: the 256 PV cell is the plain text 5-of-5 (N=5) family, whereas 384/512 share the HIGH-text N=30 lineage (HIGH-text not run at 256), so 256 stays a thin-provenance anchor; tile size is confounded with tile set (1032/487/340), so F1@20m is the cross-size headline and tile-MCC is reported per size, never differenced. BEST-ACHIEVABLE FLASH CEILING per size (consensus-only): 384 (0.814) > 512 (0.775) > 256 (0.460); single-pass 512 (0.631) > 384 (0.520) > 256 (0.342). Pro single-pass ran only at 384 (pro-text 0.792, pro-image MCC 0.868) -- context, not a tile-size comparison. Artefacts: results/tile-size-sweep/tile_size_sweep.{json,md} (now incl. Best cell per configuration at K=10: 512 px / 12.5 % F1 0.6759 [0.6239,0.7237] MCC 0.5383; 512 px / 50 % F1 0.7518 [0.7026,0.7938] MCC 0.5897; 384 px / 12.5 % F1 0.6475 [0.5935,0.6966] MCC 0.3137; 384 px / 50 % F1 0.7205 [0.6749,0.7618] MCC 0.4909. TWO STANDING PRIORS OVERTURNED. (1) 512 px wins at every overlap and every K, so the 384 px sweet spot does NOT reproduce under one footprint at T=0.7: tile-size effect -0.0824 at 12.5 % [-0.1243,-0.0429] and -0.0972 at 50 % [-0.1196,-0.0753], both excluding zero. The interaction is UNRESOLVED: difference-of-differences -0.0148 [-0.0552,+0.0268], p=0.4902, spanning zero. Bootstrap intervals here are at B=10,000 per the 2026-08-19 PI ruling (erratum E82), not the 1,000 Decision 10 pre-specified; the paired contrasts use the analysis script's own resampler, which was never on the D15 defective path, so re-running them at 10,000 moved every delta by 0.00000, every CI width by under 5 %, and no significance verdict. | h13-overlap-2026-08-18 | comparison | 3 | registered-exploratory | Results | PREDICTION SPLIT: the registered MECHANISM is confirmed, the registered PERFORMANCE claim is falsified. F1 falls monotonically as overlap rises - arm A (12.5 %) 0.5578, arm B (25 %) 0.5198, arm C (50 %) 0.4025 (common scope, 20 m, mean of 3 passes). All three paired tile-bootstrap contrasts exclude zero at B = 1,000 and B = 10,000 (A-B +0.0380, CI95 [+0.0009, +0.0708] - marginal; A-C +0.1554 [+0.1214, +0.1889]; B-C +0.1174 [+0.0922, +0.1437]). Recall behaves exactly as registered (0.7379 -> 0.7844 -> 0.8717) but precision falls faster (0.4484 -> 0.3887 -> 0.2616). The registered edge-detection analysis confirms the hypothesised mechanism and localises it: the ten mounds arm A could only ever see within 100 m of a tile edge go from recall 0.2667 (A) to 0.7667 (B) to 0.9333 (C), against 0.7468 -> 0.7847 -> 0.8706 for the other 528; arm A misses all four of the most edge-marooned mounds in all three passes and arm C finds all four. The gain is real but concentrated in under 2 % of mounds, too few to pay for the precision lost elsewhere. Cost-efficiency: every additional API dollar spent on overlap buys NEGATIVE F1 (A->B -0.1011 F1 per additional $; B->C -0.0522; arm A's $1.3708 is imputed at the measured B/C per-call rate, arms B and C are audited spend, $5.7488 total including the smoke test). The precision collapse is NOT a deduplication artefact: dedup removes 5.9-6.7 % (A), 15.7-17.9 % (B) and 39.2-40.0 % (C) of raw detections, and after removing every duplicate arm C still carries 1323.7 false positives per pass against arm A's 488.3 - each extra look is a fresh opportunity to hallucinate a mound at a new location, which no dedup rule can remove. Tile-level MCC (A 0.106, B 0.258, C 0.059) is NOT robust to the scope choice and carries no overlap claim here. Verification: scripts/verify_h13_overlap.py re-derives counts, scope, per-arm P/R/F1, cost and the edge subgroup from raw artefacts along a separate code path, 20/20 checks pass. |
